summary: Move the remaining fourteen manifest-only connectors into explicit category surfaces with health-only account enrollment and bounded host-mediated probes; do not claim domain operations.

impacts.evidence: Health-only accounts remain tenant/workspace scoped and use the existing connector-account authorization chain.
Credentials remain callback-scoped in SecretProvider; probes persist only normalized health metadata.
No public OpenAPI operation or schema migration is added.
No event type or envelope changes.
The existing Connector SDK v1 manifest and host transport are reused without a major-version change.
Generic connector accounts, secret references and health history are reused.
Probe URLs are HTTPS-only, host-validated, bounded and fail closed; credentials never enter logs or generated catalogs.
No write-sensitive domain capability is admitted; future capability promotion requires a separate reviewed qualification.
Connection checks use the existing connector account audit path and safe normalized outcomes.
No worker entity or remote write route is introduced.
Only bounded outbound health probes are added; no webhook ingress or arbitrary callback is accepted.
Timeouts, response bounds and normalized provider-unavailable reasons are enforced by the catalog probe.
The generated support rows can be disabled/reverted without data migration.
Deterministic probe, support, API and frontend tests cover the health-only boundary.
